meta.notes: day_start sets state.luck at the start of each day (Game.reset) and is the base luck value item_ladder bands below key off of (owner ruling, docs/open_tasks.md decisions log 2026-08-13). The live Rabbit's Foot/Lucky Purse amount is special_items.json's own luck_bonus effect param. Per-draft luck banding lives in item_ladder below.

The published item-count ladder ("Luck effects" DataMinedBox). Effective luck = state.luck + per-draft modifiers (special_items.luck_bonus) - state.luck_penalty (owner-ruled per-day accumulator; wiki never states its reset scope). bands[].kind: 'flat' (a flat 1-item chance), 'chain' (5-10 luck: first-match ordered list, order is load-bearing), 'variable_mix' (a variable/1-item/0-item three-way split), 'always_variable' (100% variable), 'fixed' (a deterministic item count + Luck Penalty delta). The 'chain' row with if='day1_veteran_by_fast_early_drafts' can never match in this sim: GameConfig.veteran_mode (config.py) is a plain bool with no notion of Veteran Mode having been enabled MID-RUN by fast early drafts, so that branch always falls through to the next row (see docs/open_tasks.md decisions log 2026-08-13 and the PR-A report).

"Luck effects" DataMinedBox: "Not every room rolls for luck. The rooms that don't completely skip this step, including the Luck Penalty increase. (Rooms that do roll for luck and then discard the result still increase the Luck Penalty.) The following rooms never roll for luck: [19 named rooms]." engine/items.py's roll_room_items reads this table BEFORE calling roll_ladder_count at all for a listed room -- not merely clamping the result to 0 -- so these rooms never touch state.luck_penalty, unlike every other additional_max==0 room (e.g. Lost & Found), which still rolls and discards. The wiki names 19 rooms by their base name; Closet's three Upgrade Closet variants (Hallway/Bedroom/Empty Closet, rooms.json variant_of=closet) are listed here too since they are the same room family, per the corridor/corriyard__ix50 precedent in locks.json's always_unlocked_rooms. The wiki's own prose also says "There are some rooms not on this list that only sometimes roll for luck, such as the Guess Bedroom" -- confirmed (by fetching the raw wiki source) to be a verbatim wiki typo for Guest Bedroom, NOT the sim's own unrelated 'Guess Bedroom' room (guest_bedroom__ix70, a real Guest Bedroom upgrade whose effect mimics a random other Bedroom) -- no such id belongs in this table. JUDGMENT CALL, not implemented here: the Guest Bedroom wiki page separately states 'certain upgrades disable the normal item spawns. If this happens, luck (including incrementing the Luck Penalty) does not get processed' -- this would apply to geist_bedroom__ix69 and quest_bedroom__ix71 (both additional_max=0, item spawn fully replaced by their own effects), but they are not among the wiki's named 19 and auditing every upgrade-disabled room across all 170 rooms.json records is out of scope for this table; those two variants still incorrectly roll-and-discard (bump luck_penalty) today. Report flagged for the owner.

meta.notes: Per-room transforms of the item_ladder's raw extra-item count, applied BEFORE the additional_max clamp (except one_becomes_trunk, applied at grant time on the post-clamp count -- see engine/items.py's roll_room_items). kind vocabulary: 'reduce_by_one_chance' (Nook: "There is a 20% chance to reduce the number of items by 1."), 'zero_becomes_one' (Study: "If 0 items is selected, it provides 1 item instead."), 'zero_becomes_one_or_gem' (Guest Bedroom: "If 0 items is rolled, there is a 50% chance to increase it to 1 item, or a 30% chance to spawn 1 gem." -- read as sequential/first-match, the same idiom the Luck page's own 5-10 chain and Guaranteed Item order use; not independently documented as exclusive), 'one_becomes_trunk' (Den: "If 1 item is selected, the item is always replaced with the trunk." -- instantly resolves data/special_items.json's containers.kinds.trunk.loot table via special_items.apply_grant_list rather than spawning a physical, player-opened container object; JUDGMENT CALL: every other ladder-triggered proc in this sim is an instant grant, unlike the always-present containers in Attic/Wine Cellar/etc., so this follows that convention instead of building new stateful container-placement machinery), 'not_modeled' (a documented no-op; a legitimate vocabulary member skippable for ANY room, not a per-room special case), 'deferred_ladder' (Lost & Found: "One item is added to the result, and the item count then clamped to be in 2-4" plus "If any Guaranteed Item spawns, one additional item appears, and this room does not check Luck" -- owner ruling: the published transform replaces this room's prior fixed gives=2 draw. Resolved in two stages because Lost & Found's items are a bespoke pool draw (special_items.py's lost_and_found_on_enter), not the additional_max-clamped EXTRA_ITEM_TABLE loop every other kind above feeds, and additional_max is 0 here (rooms.json) so nothing returned from this dispatcher can reach the player through the normal per-slot loop. Stage one, here: engine/items.py's _apply_count_transform stashes the raw ladder count on state.special.count_transform_raw[room.id] and returns it UNCHANGED, so the caller's min(raw, additional_max) clamp still discards it exactly as 'not_modeled' did -- no behavior change on the generic path. Stage two, special_items.py's lost_and_found_on_enter (fired later from on_enter, after this room's own guaranteed_by_room grant has run): pops the stashed raw and applies add/min/max if the room's own guaranteed item (allowance_token_lost_and_found) did NOT spawn this entry, else grants lost_and_found.gives + guaranteed_add with no luck consulted. JUDGMENT CALL: "Guaranteed Item" is mapped onto this sim's existing generic guaranteed_by_room/guaranteed_in concept (the Mora Jai Box Allowance Token) -- the wiki also describes a separate, day/rank-gated guaranteed-selection mechanic among the rare-item pool itself (Vault Key 370 / Key 8 / Upgrade Disk) that is not modeled anywhere in this sim's data and was out of scope for this ruling. Consuming the SAME stashed roll (rather than a second independent roll_ladder_count call in the hook) matters: a second roll would double the rng draw and double-count state.luck_penalty for every Lost & Found visit.

"Exact impacts on luck" DataMinedBox. "When the Dowsing Rod is used on a room, a +32 Luck bonus is applied and the standard Luck Penalty does not apply" -- read (engine/items.py's roll_dowsed_count) as: effective luck = state.luck + per-draft bonuses + rod_luck_bonus, WITHOUT subtracting state.luck_penalty (unlike roll_ladder_count's own formula); the outcome tables below still WRITE their own deltas into state.luck_penalty exactly like the ordinary ladder does, matching the wiki's closing note that repeated Dowsing use pushes ordinary future drafts toward acting 'as though a Maid's Chamber has been drafted'. regular_routine_luck_max (18) is the '18- Luck: Runs the regular non-Dowsing Rod routine' cutoff -- 'The only way to trigger this is having 4 Maid's Chambers drafted' (each is -7 directly to state.luck, engine/effects/tier1.py's anti_luck; 10 - 7*4 + 32 = 14 <= 18); engine/items.py reuses roll_ladder_count's own band logic (extracted as _roll_ladder_at) at this precomputed effective luck rather than duplicating it, then floors a 0-item result to 1 ('If it rolls 0 items, it gets increased to 1 item'). avoid_rooms (26, draft.py's slot-pick preference only) and variable_items_rooms (17, this table's own unconditional 0-2-band override) are DELIBERATELY SEPARATE published lists from each other and from never_roll_rooms above -- neither contains the other; unifying any two would silently change which rooms roll. penalty_bands key on the Dowsing Rod's OWN per-day Dowsing Penalty counter (state.dowsing_penalty, distinct from state.luck_penalty, 'does not impact anything outside this effect'), each band's outcomes weighted-percentage: 'one' = 1 item; 'variable' = defer to item_ladder.variable at this SAME effective luck ('In almost all cases (without 4 Maid's Chambers), "variable items" means 5% for 3 items ... 95% for 2 items' -- item_ladder.variable's own 17+ row already collapses to exactly that at the luck levels Dowsing produces, and the general Luck page table it inherits from correctly covers the rare low-luck 4-Maid's-Chambers case too); 'fixed' = the 0-2 band's explicit 3-/4-item rows, each writing BOTH state.luck_penalty (the 'standard' one, per the wiki's own '+2 Luck Penalty'/'+3 Luck Penalty' phrasing) and state.dowsing_penalty; 'recurse_0_2' (3-5 band only, its own 20% row) re-runs the FULL 0-2 band procedure -- the variable_items_rooms check AND the regular_routine_luck_max check AND its weighted table, not just the last of the three -- 'run as though it was 0-2 Dowsing Penalty' is read as the whole section, not one row of it. Row-kind vocabulary: {one, variable, fixed, recurse_0_2}; tools/validate_data.py checks each band's p_pct sums to exactly 100. Owner ruling (docs/open_tasks.md decisions log 2026-08-13): Dowsing BYPASSES the additional_max clamp entirely (engine/items.py's roll_room_items) -- without this the whole ladder collapses to ~1 item and the item is pointless. NOT modelled (named gaps, out of scope): the Shelter interaction (a dowsed Lavatory/Furnace should count as sheltered; this sim's Shelter is a global day counter, not a per-room mark), the Coat Check/Compass quirk, real-time 'premature drafting' animation artifacts, and outer-room (West Path Shop) drafts, which use their own separate deal pipeline (game.py's _deal_outer_options) that this feature does not hook.

main_course_cycle indexed by day % 5: index 0 = pizza (day%5==0), index 1 = salmon (day%5==1), etc. fruit_weights ordering (apple > banana > orange) is sourced from the wiki's Pantry description; the exact weight values are not published and are inferred.
